summary_override.summary_en: EmoHarness uses a Builder to revise prompts, settings and restricted verification code from a frozen student model’s failure traces. A separate validation split decides whether a candidate replaces the current Harness for later rounds. Most gains come from audio evidence, and the incremental evolution gains do not survive multiple-comparison correction. Human developers inspected some evaluation items, so the evaluation is not an untouched holdout.

evidence.quote: A harness is a bundle of prompts, settings files, and verification code.

Given the incumbent’s files, intermediate records, clustered failures, and earlier proposals with check and reviewer feedback, the Builder proposes up to four candidate harnesses, each an edit aimed at one failure cluster; evaluation data are never exposed.
Second, gates on a separate validation split decide promotion, and the Builder sees neither validation scores nor gate decisions, only the resulting harness.
Held-out refers to task type, not to an untouched test set: 986 evaluation items, which we cannot identify, were inspected during development.
Most of the boost comes from audio-derived evidence

summary_override.summary_en: LASER represents observation skills as structured instructions and uses discrepancies between generated and reference captions to revise a responsible field or add a skill. A candidate replaces the library only when it improves caption quality without increasing contradictions on a selection set containing different videos. Later rounds reuse the accepted library. Model parameters stay fixed, and evaluation freezes the library; the evidence concerns video object-state description.
summary_override.summary_zh: LASER把观察技能表示为结构化指令，根据生成描述与参考描述的差异，修订负责的指令字段或增建技能。候选在不同视频组成的选择集上改善描述质量且不增加矛盾时才替换技能库，后续轮次复用；模型参数保持固定，最终评测冻结技能库。证据限定于视频物体状态描述。

evidence.quote: An observation skill is a structured textual instruction that tells the agent what to inspect about an object and how to describe the visual evidence.
For a discrepancy linked to an existing skill, the MLLM proposes an edit to one responsible field; if no skill covers the situation, it proposes a new skill.

The accepted candidate with the highest caption quality replaces the current library; if none is accepted, the library is retained.
The resulting skill library remains fixed during evaluation.
Selection requires an improvement in caption quality without increasing reference contradictions.
Feedback-guided skill revision improves observation instructions using existing reference captions while keeping model parameters fixed.

summary_override.summary_en: SAT uses a teacher to write reusable procedural skills from student failure traces and diagnostic probes. Positive utility on development tasks governs admission or replacement of generic skills. After the teacher leaves, the fixed student and base executor reuse the library on later tasks. Benefits depend on the student and delivery method. Evaluation covers new instances of task families seen during preparation, not arbitrary domain transfer.
summary_override.summary_zh: SAT教师根据学生的失败轨迹和诊断探测，编写可复用的程序性技能指令；开发任务上的正效用决定技能是否入库或替换通用技能。教师退出后，固定学生与执行框架在后续任务中继续使用技能库。收益依赖学生及技能投递方式，验证范围是准备阶段已见任务族的新实例，不能外推为任意领域迁移。

evidence.quote: SAT treats teaching as an iterative loop between a stronger teacher and a fixed learner (Figure 1 ).
In each round the student attempts teaching tasks, and the teacher updates its model of the student, tests it with diagnostic probes, and writes candidate skills that must pass an admission test.
The teacher proposes up to three candidate skills per round, each a short natural-language procedure with a target category and applicability metadata (Appendix A ).
A candidate with positive utility enters the library and may replace a generic skill in its category.
After preparation the teacher is removed.
We study this question with skills that the harness supplies as advisory context, keeping the model weights and harness code fixed.
The gain is realized when the delivery route suits the student and the student can execute procedures.
with later instances drawn from task families seen during preparation.

summary_override.summary_en: RoboACE alternates revisions to curriculum-selection and execution Harnesses around frozen foundation models. Optimizers inspect independent-run feedback, revise prompts, tool interfaces and procedural skills, and compare versions on fixed task snapshots before retention. The qualifying objects are the selection and execution methods, not the curriculum tasks themselves. Results cover one development trajectory and fixed panels within the LIBERO ecosystem; final evaluation does not select versions.

summary_override.summary_en: FGSE turns execution experience into bounded prompt or tool-policy patches with explicit preconditions. It tests temporary changes on transfer, falsification and archived regression probes before committing, narrowing the scope and retrying, or rejecting them. Accepted changes are reused on later tasks and can be removed from retrieval after violations. Inclusion is limited to the explicit prompt/tool-policy branch, not all memory content; theoretical guarantees depend on the stated assumptions.
summary_override.summary_zh: FGSE把执行经验转为带适用前提的有限提示或工具策略补丁，在临时状态下测试迁移、反例和历史回归，再提交、缩小适用范围重试或拒绝。通过的行为修改在后续任务中复用，出现违例可停止检索。这里只收录明确的提示/工具策略修改分支，不把所有记忆内容都算作Harness；理论保证依赖论文所列假设。

evidence.quote: The behavior field specifies a bounded prompt/tool-policy patch.
Hypotheses with localized failures are refined once through precondition narrowing and reevaluated; hypotheses that still fail are rejected.

A committed hypothesis is stored together with its precondition, behavior change, verifier, evaluated probes, verifier outcomes, and post-commit violation record. Rejected hypotheses are excluded from retrievable memory.
During future inference, FGSE retrieves committed hypotheses whose preconditions match the current interaction state and whose violation records remain below threshold.
Post-commit violations update a running violation score; hypotheses exceeding the violation threshold are removed from retrieval.
The only properties needed are boundedness and conditional independence of the final evaluation samples for each fixed

summary_override.summary_en: NCP studies verified admission and persistence of external control rules. Execution telemetry generates candidates, and a verifier binds evidence to the rule and current policy version before admission or rejection; temporary weight interventions are restored after each request. All candidates were rejected in the actual microbenchmark, leaving the active policy and final outputs unchanged. This is control-layer framework and negative-result evidence; promotion in controlled tests does not establish self-improvement on real tasks.
summary_override.summary_zh: NCP研究外部控制规则的验证准入与持久化：执行遥测生成候选规则，验证器将结果绑定到规则和当前策略版本，再决定采用或拒绝；每次请求结束恢复临时权重干预。真实微基准里所有候选都被拒绝，活动策略和最终结果均未改变。它提供控制层框架及负结果证据，受控测试中的晋升不代表真实任务实现了自我改进。

summary_override.summary_en: Before task learning, RoboScript segments the collected demonstrations and asks a coding agent to write environment-specific skills for gaps in the existing action interface. An independent driver replays the skills, checks transfer across layouts, and rechecks gains against regressions. Coverage feedback drives further rounds before the skill library is frozen for later tasks. Inclusion is limited to this executable tool-skill construction and selection loop, separate from ordinary Task Memory content updates. The paper does not isolate the contribution of skill construction, and continual failure-driven skill creation during deployment remains future work.
summary_override.summary_zh: RoboScript 在任务学习前把汇集的示范拆为动作片段，将现有接口无法覆盖的缺口交给 coding agent 编写环境技能。独立 driver 回放、检查跨布局复用并复查新增技能的得失，按覆盖反馈迭代后冻结技能库，供后续任务调用。这里仅将可执行工具技能的构建与筛选闭环纳入 Harness；普通 Task Memory 内容更新另计。论文未单独量化技能构建的贡献，部署中遇到失败再持续生成新技能仍是未来工作。

evidence.quote: Action interface with receipts. The agent acts through a three-layer API. Shared entry points for grasping, placing, corrective motions, reachability checks, and coordinated bimanual motion are environment-independent. An environment binding discovered by automated probes supplies coordinate frames, joint limits, table height, and gripper characteristics. Before learning, the agent builds environment-specific skills on these two layers. It segments each demonstration into action primitives, identifies which segments the existing entries cannot explain, and hands each gap to a coding agent that writes a skill. A driver validates each skill by running it on the demonstration scene and checking that it transfers to other layouts without encoding any absolute position. The loop repeats until coverage stops improving, and the final skill set is frozen before task learning.
evidence.section: PDF page 6; Section 4.1, Action interface with receipts

evidence.quote: Shared and environment-specific skills. Skills are divided by whether they depend on the environment. Shared entry points cover common operations such as observing, grasping, placing, corrective motions, reachability checks, arm selection, and coordinated bimanual motion. These entry points hold no convention of any environment. Environment conventions, including coordinate frames, end-effector-to-fingertip offsets, gripper normalization, the collision world, and arm names, enter the shared entry points as data through a binding. An operation that holds only in a particular environment is an environment-specific skill, and it becomes visible only when that environment is loaded.
evidence.section: PDF page 17; Appendix C.1, Shared and environment-specific skills

evidence.quote: Coverage of the demonstrations. Skill building starts from the demonstrations of all tasks. Each demonstration is cut at its gripper events into segments of seven kinds, namely grasp, place, carry, touch, release, move, and return home. A segment is explained when an existing entry point or written skill, with parameters fitted to the demonstration, reproduces it from the state where the segment starts. Each task is checked in two ways. Every segment is replayed from its own start, and the plan of the whole task is also rolled out once from the reset, so that each call starts where the previous calls left the scene. Segments that no entry explains are gaps, and gaps of the same kind and failure class are grouped into clusters.
evidence.section: PDF page 17; Appendix C.2, Coverage of the demonstrations

evidence.quote: Written skills. Each cluster is handed to a coding agent that works in a sandbox with fixed budgets of case runs, wall-clock time, and tokens. A written skill has two parts. The action part runs at the deployable tier, exactly as the agent runs it in rehearsal and deployment, and it uses only the action API, the object handles it receives, and its parameters. The fitting part runs only during skill building and may read the recording and the ground-truth scene. It returns the parameters that reproduce one segment. These parameters hold no absolute position, since the fit is repeated on the demonstration moved across the table and a parameter that moves with it by more than 1 cm rejects the fit.
evidence.section: PDF page 17; Appendix C.2, Written skills

evidence.quote: Gate. The driver accepts a skill only through its own checks and never relies on the report of the coding agent. A static check rejects imports outside an allowed set, task names, object labels, and position literals. The skill must then explain the gaps it was written for. A transfer check runs its fitted parameters on the same segment of up to three other demonstrations whose object lies at least 5 cm away, and rejects a skill that explains none of them, so that a replay cannot pass as a skill. Finally, all sweeps of the round run again with the accepted skills and the candidates, and a candidate is dropped when its confirmed losses outweigh its gains. Every process that imports a written skill runs in the sandbox.

Stopping and freezing. Rounds repeat until coverage stops growing, measured by explained segments, task rollouts that reach the end, official successes of the rolled-out plans, and completed stages. The accepted skills are then frozen as the skill set of the environment. The task plans that the builder uses to measure coverage stay in its records and never enter the skill set, a Task Memory, or any input of learning or deployment.
evidence.section: PDF page 18; Appendix C.2, Stopping and freezing

evidence.quote: Benchmark and protocol. RoboTwin 2.0 [11] defines 50 dual-arm tasks in a clean setting (fixed background) and a randomized setting (randomized textures, lighting, table height, and distractors). The agent first builds its skill set across all 50 tasks, then learns each task from one automatically selected clean demonstration, with rehearsal on clean scenes only. The frozen Task Memory is evaluated in both settings with the official server, unseen instructions, and the official step limit. Each task is evaluated on 10 episodes per setting (1,000 episodes total), as each episode requires dozens of model calls. We report success rate averaged over all tasks, the mean of the two settings, and retention (randomized divided by clean).
evidence.section: PDF page 8; Section 5.1, Benchmark and protocol

evidence.quote: Baselines. Trained action policies (VLAs and WAMs) are trained on all 50 tasks with 50 clean demonstrations per task and evaluated on 100 episodes. The agent-with-policy baseline is HarnessVLA [93], which orchestrates a fine-tuned VLA with a coding agent. All baseline results come from the official leaderboard [11] or published reports, excluding policies trained on randomized data.

Tab. 2 removes one component at a time. Deployment ablations use the frozen memory from the main run, the second group builds a memory without interacting with the world, and learning ablations relearn every memory from scratch. All groups use the same 10 tasks covering all five categories, with 10 episodes per task in each setting on shared seeds, so all comparisons are paired and we report exact McNemar p values.
evidence.section: PDF page 10; Section 5.4, Where Do the Gains Come From?

Future work. Beyond these limitations, the agentic side of WICL remains largely unexplored. Agents could build new skills when existing ones fail, coordinate several specialized agents over a long task, or rehearse in learned world models when no simulator is available. Our results also suggest that agent-centric embodied models are a promising direction. A foundation model trained to use embodied tools, read physical feedback, and maintain a task memory could make WICL faster, cheaper, and more reliable than general-purpose models accessed through an API.
evidence.section: PDF page 24; Appendix F, Future work
